item.title: Carrick-on-Shannon's flood-defence scheme to go to planning in 2026
item.description: Carrick-on-Shannon's 30-million-euro flood-defence scheme will go to planning in 2026. The project has been worked on for several years, after the town was badly affected by flooding in 2009 and 2015. It will involve embankments and other flood-defence systems along the Shannon. Advertisement Leitrim County Council chief executive, Joseph Gilhooly, says it will go to planning in the first half of 2026 and be finished around five years later.

item.title: Baby girl among first born at Portiuncula University Hospital in 2026
item.description: One of the first babies born in Ireland this year has been named. Baby Asqa Samad was born to parents Farzana and Afsal in Portiuncula University Hospital in County Galway. The little girl was welcomed at 1.21 this morning. Advertisement Elsewhere, Milly Elizabeth Kelleher arrived at 40 seconds past midnight in the National Maternity Hospital, while a baby boy was delivered just after half past twelve in the Rotunda.

item.title: Cold snap may bring frost, ice and snow to region this week
item.description: A cold snap is set to hit the Shannonside region this week, with frost, ice, freezing fog and snow in places. The worst of the icy conditions is expected across parts of north Connacht and Ulster, with snow likely on higher ground from tomorrow into Saturday. Temperatures could drop as low as minus five degrees in some inland areas, and daytime highs will struggle to rise above freezing in parts of the north and north-west. item.title: New bridge between Carrick-on-Shannon and Cootehall to go to tender in 2026
item.description: Plans for a new bridge between Carrick-on-Shannon and Cootehall will go to tender early in 2026. Up to 5 million euro will be spent on a replacement for Hartley Bridge. It's around two miles outside Carrick and three miles from Cootehall village. Advertisement The current bridge is over 100 years old and Leitrim County Council chief executive, Joseph Gilhooly, says it's in poor condition.

item.title: EU to vote on Mercosur trade agreement in new year amid beef import concerns
item.description: The EU will vote in the new year whether or not to approve the Mercusor trade agreement. If passed, the deal will allow 99,000 tonnes carcass weight of beef from South America enter the EU at a much reduced tariff rate of 7.5 per cent. The quantity of beef under this quota will be phased in over a five-year period. Advertisement Sinn Féin's agriculture spokesperson, Martin Kenny, a Sligo-Leitrim TD disagrees with the proposals.

item.title: Ireland West Airport records busiest year to date
item.description: Ireland West Airport say that 2025 has been their busiest year to date. Close to 950,000 passengers have used the regional airport this year. There are currently 22 destinations that people can fly to from the airport, with London the most popular. Advertisement Head of Marketing at Ireland West Airport, Donal Healy, says around 110,000 extra passengers travelled from Knock this year.

item.title: Ambulances at the scene of two-car crash on Carrick-Boyle road
item.description: Two ambulances are at the scene of a crash on the N4 between Carrick-on-Shannon and Boyle. Two cars collided around Ardcarne while travelling in the direction of Carrick. Gardai are also at the scene of the crash, which happened at around 4pm. Advertisement Gardai said: "No injuries were reported at the time."
